title: KV260 BD wrapper build — synth+opt pass, place_design blocked by XCK26 resource overflow at N_SPINS=128
retro_070_resolution_note: BD wrapper built, sub-IP synth + opt_design passed cleanly, no I/O planning DRC errors. The block design topology is correct; bitstream is blocked by a separate (sizing) issue, not by the board-integration wrapper that was RETRO-070's concern.
retro_new_suggested_title: KV260 Ising sampler design exceeds XCK26 resource budget at N_SPINS=128 — need parametric build at N_SPINS<=64 to fit PL
retro_new_suggested_root_cause: hardware/kv260/ising_sampler_v2.v parameterises N_SPINS=128 and MAX_DEGREE=32 by default. The parallel adder trees (h_eff[N_SPINS] with MAX_DEGREE fan-in each) plus the sigmoid LUT inference ladder produce ~290k LUT6 instances at those values, roughly 2.5x the XCK26 PL budget of 117k LUT6. The 128-spin target was appropriate for larger Zynq parts (XCU250 and up); KV260's XCK26 needs a smaller configuration.
retro_new_suggested_fix_options: A: Override N_SPINS and MAX_DEGREE at BD instantiation time in hardware/kv260/build_bd.tcl via set_property CONFIG.N_SPINS / CONFIG.MAX_DEGREE on the ising_sampler_0 cell. No RTL edit required because the RTL is already parameterised. Target first: N_SPINS=64, MAX_DEGREE=16 (projected ~73k LUT6, fits). (~5 LOC change, already landed in build_bd.tcl on this commit)

B: Time-multiplex coupling evaluations across fewer DSPs (rewrite h_eff combinational adder trees as sequential state machine with N_STEPS_PER_UPDATE > 1). Produces the full 128-spin result at the cost of ~128/MAX_PAR cycles per update. Non-trivial RTL rewrite, ~300 LOC.
C: Move to a larger SoC (ZCU102/104, XCVU9P dev kit). Not available locally, defers the KV260 track.
retro_new_suggested_next_step: Re-run hardware/kv260/build_bd.tcl with CARNOT_N_SPINS=64 CARNOT_MAX_DEGREE=16 in the environment (the defaults are already set to those values on this commit). Record actual post-opt utilisation in results/kv260_bd_build_N64.json so the projected-vs-actual table stays honest. If N=64 still overshoots, step down to N=32 and repeat.
